title: Blygger 0.3 shared definitions
description: Shared $defs for the 0.3 publication surface (docs/protocol-v0.3.md). MUST-level constraints only; SHOULD/RECOMMENDED live in advisory.schema.json (decision #48: MUST fails, SHOULD warns, MAY is shape-checked when present).

id.description: §5.1: 128 random bits as 26 chars of lowercase Crockford base32 (alphabet 0-9a-z minus i l o u). Decisions #2, #16.

utc.description: §4: every protocol timestamp is ISO 8601 UTC ending in Z; a publisher MUST NOT write local time into any protocol surface.

version.description: §5.2: positive integer, +1 per publish event; a bare counter (decision #19).

contentHash.description: §5.1: "sha256:" + hex(SHA-256(content_md as UTF-8)). Recomputed by the semantic rule hash.matches-content_md.

origin.description: §5.9/§12.2: a target's identity origin — the post-redirect manifest URL minus blyg.json, so it ends in '/'. Decisions #14, #17.

author.description: §5.5 (decision #11): OPTIONAL, opaque, client-asserted pass-through. Readers MUST accept any object; `name` RECOMMENDED, `url` OPTIONAL, any other members are the client's private authorspace grammar. Only the object type is checked.

url.description: §5.5: OPTIONAL. Identity practice (decision #35) recommends a URL the person controls.

cited.description: §5.9 (decision #30): the human half of a citation — self-asserted, frozen when the reference was made, never verified, never baked into content_html. Also permitted on a {url} stub (§16.1a, decision #55; ruled, next revision).

retrieved.description: §5.9: REQUIRED whenever cited is present — a citation without a date is not a citation (decision #30).

source.description: §5.9: OPTIONAL — the target blyg's title as seen.

author.description: §5.9: OPTIONAL — the target's own author.name passed through (§5.5, decision #11).

excerpt.description: §5.9: OPTIONAL caption, not a quotation; publishers SHOULD cap near 200 chars (advisory layer).

url.description: §5.9: OPTIONAL — the target's page as it stood. For forked_from the cited target is a pin, whose human page is {page}v{n}/ (§8.4, decision #24).

selector.description: §10.3 (decision #49): W3C Web Annotation text-quote selector on a partial transclusion entry. Ignored by verification; readers MAY ignore.

exact.description: §10.3: REQUIRED — the selection, normalized by §10.2's text-content rule; MUST be a substring of the target snapshot's text content at the baked version (§10.2).

referenceCore.description: §5.9: the reference shape shared by forked_from, stub_of and transclusions[] — origin/id/version is the whole machine-readable identity; cited (and, on transclusions, selector) are the only other members.

version.description: §5.9: the version the publisher actually saw and, for a transclusion, baked.

absoluteReference.description: §5.6 rule 1 / §10.6: a reference whose origin is REQUIRED even when it is the publisher's own — a citation is absolute (decisions #27, #26). No other members than origin/id/version/cited (§5.9: "and nothing else").

transclusion.description: §10.3: one transclusions[] entry; origin omitted for own-origin sources (decision #26), present for remote; OPTIONAL selector for a partial transclusion (decision #49).

stubOf.description: §10.6 (decision #27): exactly one target — a blyg reference with origin REQUIRED, or {url} for a plain-web target. cited on {url} is ruled (§16.1a, #55) and accepted here.

cited.description: §16.1a (decision #55): ruled, enters §10.6 once a client emits it.

generatedEntry.description: §5.7 (decision #20, #37): one generated span's provenance. MUST NOT carry instruction text or other pre-generation authoring state (rule 2).

sources.description: §5.7 rule 1: exact published versions of this origin's items drawn on; MAY be empty (no sources declared). At 0.3 a source is own-origin and carries no origin member (remote sources are 0.4, §16.3, decision #44).

changelogEntry.description: §5.2: metadata only — version, time, optional note, optional pinned:true — never diffs or content.

note.description: §5.2: describes a change; where the prior version is unpinned it MUST NOT reproduce it (not machine-checkable).

pinned.description: §5.2/§8: present only as true on pinned versions.

generated.description: §16.6c (decision #40): ruled, not yet normative — the studio wrote the note.

media.description: §5.4: a media object referenced by the item.

url.description: §5.4: relative to the origin or absolute; a structured field readers resolve (unaffected by #53).
